title: Second Constable's History (Português)
summary: The Second Constable related his chronicle: [PT]
full_text:
The Second Constable related his chronicle:

'A series of midnight burglaries baffled the silversmiths’ quarter; the thief left no trace and scaled thirty-foot walls without ropes.

I did not station noisy guards in the streets. I secretly dusted the tops of all the garden walls and alley roofs with a fine powder of white flour and ground chalk.

At dawn, we followed a clear trail of white footprints from the roof of the robbed goldsmith’s shop directly across the terraces to the attic window of an acrobat who lived beside the city gate!

We recovered all the stolen silver from beneath his floorboards, proving that subtle preparation catches the swiftest thief.'
moral: A quiet, patient trap catches the burglar where noisy searches fail. [PT]
